CausalChain: Dual-targeted nanoparticle delivers boronated agent selectively to tumor cells and TAMs -> BNCT irradiation produces high LET particles causing localized damage -> simultaneous ablation of tumor cells and depletion of immunosuppressive macrophages -> release of damage-associated molecular patterns and tumor antigens -> activation of dendritic cells and T-cell priming -> enhanced systemic anti-tumor immune response and induction of abscopal effects
Hypothesis: Conjugating boronated compounds to dual-targeting nanoparticles that selectively localize to both tumor cells and tumor-associated macrophages can, upon BNCT irradiation, not only achieve precise tumor cell destruction but also remodel the tumor microenvironment to activate systemic anti-tumor immunity and promote abscopal effects.
Abstract: This review explores the potential for an innovative dual-targeted approach in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) by combining traditional tumor cell irradiation with selective targeting of immunosuppressive cells within the tumor microenvironment. Emerging evidence suggests that BNCT’s high linear energy transfer (LET) radiation not only destroys tumor cells but can also induce the release of tumor antigens, a process that may be amplified by simultaneous depletion of tumor-supportive immune subsets. In this hypothesis, we propose conjugating boronated compounds to nanoparticles engineered with ligands targeting both tumor-specific markers and receptors overexpressed on tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). The dual targeting is anticipated to concentrate boron in both malignant cells and immunosuppressive stromal components of the tumor. Subsequent neutron irradiation would then lead to local ablation and reprogramming of the tumor microenvironment, thereby enhancing antitumor immune responses and possibly eliciting abscopal effects. This paradigm opens new avenues for combined radiobiological and immunomodulatory effects in BNCT, paving the way for improved therapeutic outcomes in resistant cancers.
